title: Recording Kimmeridgian Palaeoclimate Changes Using Biofacial and Isotopic Analyses of Benthic Foraminifers From Normandy (Northwest France)
content:
Abstract

During the Kimmeridgian, the Wealdian Basin experienced several periodic disaerobic events, interpreted as the result of extensive rainfall patterns, high sea level and moderate stratification of the water column. These events are recorded in different regions of UK and France. The studied Kimmeridgian strata exposed North of le Havre city reveal the presence of thin layers of marls and clays, rich in well-diversified and well-preserved benthic foraminiferal assemblages. These sections provide excellent material for analysing the response of benthic foraminiferal assemblages to climate fluctuations of the late Jurassic. Lithological observations together with biofacial and biometric analyses of benthic foraminifers have been carried out to investigate the Kimmeridgian dysoxic events and their effect on the microbenthos. The foraminiferal association recorded in the organic-rich interval of the studied succession is dominated by small specimens of the genus Lenticulina, a taxon which is able to survive under oxygen-depleted environment. Alongside the observed size-decrease of lenticulinids, a diminished benthic foraminiferal assemblage as well as increasing TOC and HI values indicate the development of a dysoxic environment at the sea floor. At the same time, carbon and oxygen isotope records on well-preserved tests of the genus Lenticulina indicate increasing temperatures (decreasing δ18O Lenticulina ) and decreasing δ13C Lenticulina values indicative of decreasing oxygenation of the sea floor and/or increased productivity. Overall, the dataset infers the development of humid conditions and a deminished water-column mixing during the Kimmeridgian. This phenomenon might be intensified by the palaeogeographic configuration of the western European shelf and severely impacted life on the sea-floor.
